statements.t: We plan to become the tech-enabled leader in the $800 billion building products distribution and installation industry and are targeting $50 billion in annual revenues within the next decade through accretive acquisitions, including tuck-in acquisitions with the potential for significant bottom-line contributions, and organic growth initiatives.
In addition, we believe there will continue to be opportunities to purchase small businesses on accretive terms.

By combining traditional building supplies with engineered components, including trusses and wall panels, installation services and field management capabilities, we are able to help customers address labor shortages, simplify procurement, improve project coordination and reduce delays.
Trailing 12-month TRI-BUILT sales were $943 million, all at legacy Beacon, and our target is to grow TRI-BUILT to more than $2 billion in sales over the next three years.
We believe technology will help us accelerate many of these improvements in the coming months.
We expect these new platforms to support the vast majority of revenue across the three acquired businesses by the end of 2027.
We also expect improvements in routing, load planning, and replenishment to reduce transportation costs and working capital requirements while maintaining customer fulfillment.
A third of our regions have exceeded our 95% on-time delivery target, demonstrating the opportunity to replicate these improvements across the network.

In considering our need for a valuation allowance, we consider our historical and future projected taxable income, as well as other objectively verifiable evidence, including our realization of tax attributes and utilization of net operating loss carryforwards.
We believe that it is at least more likely than not that the benefit of the year-to-date losses will be realized in future periods.

We have not reconciled our Adjusted EBITDA target to net income, the most directly comparable GAAP measure, because we cannot predict without unreasonable efforts the outcome of certain items that are necessary for the reconciliation, including future acquisitions, stock-based compensation, transaction and transformation costs, and provision for (benefit from) income taxes, the impact of which could be significant.
In general, we expect our net sales and net income to be the highest in quarters ending June 30, September 30, and December 31, which represent the peak months of construction and re-roofing.

Conversely, we expect low net income levels or net losses in quarters ending March 31, when winter construction cycles and cold weather patterns have an adverse impact on our customers’ ability to conduct their business.

Dividends on the Series C Preferred Stock will be payable on a quarterly basis in cash and/or by delivery of shares of registered (or freely tradeable) common stock, in each case at the sole discretion of the Company.

Upon the occurrence of a fundamental change of the Company (i) in certain circumstances, the Company will be obligated to pay a customary fundamental change make-whole premium on the Series C Preferred Stock converted in connection with such fundamental change by increasing the conversion rate on such Series C Preferred Stock and (ii) the Company will be obligated to offer to redeem all of the Series C Preferred…
We serve 194,000 customers across the legacy Beacon, Kodiak, and TopBuild businesses, but typically supply only a portion of what they need for a project.
Our people will be able to provide quotes faster, check inventory in real time, and respond to customers more quickly.

“We’re on track to reach $4 billion in adjusted EBITDA by 2030 from the businesses we already own and $50 billion in annual revenue within the decade through organic growth and disciplined acquisitions.”

risks related to maintaining our safety record
liability exposure due to the nature and breadth of our installation services operations, including from construction defect and warranty claims

seasonality, weather-related conditions and natural disasters

the risk that Mr. Jacobs’ past performance may not be representative of future results

the development of alternatives to distributors in the supply chain and competitive pricing pressure from customers
changes in building codes and consumer preferences that could affect our ability to market our service offerings
risks associated with periodic litigation, regulatory proceedings and enforcement actions
the impact of legislative, regulatory, economic, competitive and technological changes
risks related to insurance and bonding, including the use of a wholly owned insurance captive to manage risks
unknown liabilities and uncertainties regarding general economic, business, competitive, legal, regulatory, tax and geopolitical conditions; and

other factors, including those set forth in the Company’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, including its most recent Annual Report on Form 10-K and any subsequent Quarterly Reports on Form 10-Q
